In this VladTV interview, Rainwater revisits tense moments involving Mo3, Errol Spence Jr., and Yella Beezy in Dallas. He explains his version of the gas station encounter where Spence allegedly sped off and crashed his Ferrari near the Dallas County Jail, while Mo3 continued home. Rainwater also details the January 2020 incident outside V Live nightclub, claiming he was jumped, injured, and robbed of his watch, leading to a civil lawsuit against Yella Beezy.

Rainwater says Mo3’s reaction was blunt—telling him to “go get your money”—and recalls earlier conflict with Yella Beezy dating back to a 2014 Kevin Gates concert in Dallas. He also discusses courtroom footage, the failed settlement offer, and a jury award he says totaled $375,000, with efforts underway to collect royalties.

Former DEA agent Chris Feistl details his 12-plus years in Colombia across three tours, from the fall of the Cali Cartel to investigations targeting the North Valley Cartel, AUC paramilitaries, FARC, ELN, and other armed groups. Speaking with Vlad, Feistl explains how Colombian traffickers shifted cocaine routes through Mexico, believing they could avoid U.S. extradition—only to face American conspiracy indictments as drugs continued reaching the United States.  

The conversation covers the violent North Valley power struggle after Orlando Henao, including Diego Montoya “Don Diego” and Wilber Varela “Jabón,” whose war left thousands dead. Feistl also discusses the FBI’s role, Colombian security forces, Venezuela as a refuge for traffickers, and the endless cycle of cartel leadership replacements. He closes by reflecting on retiring from the DEA in 2014 and moving into private-sector anti-money laundering work.

In this VladTV interview, Jimmy DiModica details how he says he stepped into control of Laborers Local 342 in Newark, New Jersey, after his father, a Gambino crime family figure in NJ, was sidelined by a parole violation tied to a Maryland arrest. DiModica discusses the fallout from Bobby Cabot’s conviction, the previous business manager Tony, and how a power vacuum inside the union allegedly allowed him to deal directly with contractors.

He breaks down his claimed system for labor racketeering: charging percentages on construction jobs, using non-union “scab” labor, manipulating shop steward reports, and collecting cash to help contractors avoid benefits and pension payments. DiModica also recalls a tense Route 17 lunch involving a contractor, a Pagans-connected associate, and a threat over unpaid money. A firsthand look at organized crime, union corruption, and construction industry intimidation in New Jersey.

--------
In this VladTV interview, John Franzese Jr. reflects on becoming a confidential witness, wearing a wire for the FBI, and the emotional toll of recording his father, Colombo crime family figure John “Sonny” Franzese. He discusses more than 400 hours of conversations, working with agent Rob Lewicki, and the 2008 federal racketeering indictment involving Sonny Franzese and acting boss Thomas Gioeli. Franzese Jr. recalls testifying in Brooklyn federal court in 2010, identifying his 93-year-old father on the stand, and processing the eight-year sentence that followed for extortion, loan sharking, and crimes tied to strip clubs and a Long Island pizzeria. He also addresses family fallout, rumors of a hit, his brother Michael’s criticism, and why he says he believed cooperating was the right decision despite the personal cost. A candid look inside one of the most painful turns in modern Mafia history.

--------
Chris Feistl breaks down the fall of the Cali Cartel after the surrender of Pacho Herrera in 1996, detailing Colombian National Police raids, prison trafficking, and the return of extradition in Colombia after December 17, 1997. The conversation traces how evidence from the Southern District of Florida and Southern District of New York led to U.S. indictments against Gilberto and Miguel Rodríguez Orejuela, who were later extradited, sentenced to 30 years, and tied to a $2.1 billion forfeiture agreement.

Feistl also discusses the escape and death of Chepe Santacruz, the alleged role of Carlos Castaño, and the rise of the North Valley Cartel as violence spread through Medellín, Bogotá, Cali, and the Buenaventura port corridor. From prison murders to cartel power struggles, this interview examines the aftermath of one of Colombia’s most powerful cocaine empires.

In this VladTV interview, Rainwater details the Dallas tension involving comedian Roy Lee, Yella Beezy, and Mo3, explaining how internet jokes about Oak Cliff, North Dallas, and McKinney escalated into real-life violence. Rainwater says he introduced Roy Lee to Mo3 after seeing how artists and comedians like T.I. and Lil Duval connected, but claims Roy’s jokes about Yella Beezy led to him being jumped twice, including an incident at King of Diamonds involving Beezy’s circle and Joey Bodega.

Rainwater recalls Roy Lee being shot on September 25, 2018, saying Roy called him from the ambulance and later told him someone around Yella Beezy was responsible. He also describes visiting Roy with Mo3, Roy’s recovery at home, and the blood clot complications that led to his death on October 13, 2018. The conversation covers Dallas rap beef, street politics, and the aftermath of Roy Lee’s passing.

--------
In this VladTV interview, Jimmy DiModica recounts the years before his labor union involvement, describing a three-year run across the U.S. with what he calls a “precision” theft crew led by a master thief. DiModica details how distractions were used in regular stores—not just jewelry shops—from Kennebunkport, Maine, and Lake Geneva, Wisconsin, to Ocean City, Maryland, Detroit, Chicago, and Florida. He recalls one Circle K score where money was allegedly hidden in an old sneaker, and explains how the operation finally came under scrutiny after a Maryland pharmacy incident. DiModica also discusses being linked to the case through his father, the role of surveillance footage, the legal “Stet” outcome, and hiring the law office of Peter Angelos, former Baltimore Orioles owner. The conversation also touches on Milford Academy, the Baltimore Colts connection, and how this chapter led toward the union world.
